# AF 第七章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 7

[P01] It was a bitter winter. Stormy（暴风雨） weather came, then sleet（雨夹雪） and snow, and then a hard frost（霜） that did not break until well into February. The animals went on as best they could with the rebuilding of the windmill（风车）. They knew well that the outside world was watching them, and that envious（嫉妒的） humans would be glad and triumph（胜利） if the mill（磨坊） was not finished on time. Out of spite（恶意）, the humans pretended not to believe that it was Snowball who had destroyed the windmill. They said it had fallen down because the walls were too thin. The animals knew this was not true.

[P02] Still, they had decided to build the walls three feet thick this time, not eighteen inches like before, which meant gathering（聚集） much bigger quantities（数量） of stone. For a long time the quarry（采石场） was full of snowdrifts（雪堆） and they could do nothing. They made some progress in the dry frosty（霜冷的） weather that followed, but it was cruel work, and the animals did not feel so hopeful（有希望） as before. They were always cold, and usually hungry too. Only Boxer and Clover never lost heart. Squealer made excellent speeches on the joy of service and the dignity（尊严） of labour（劳作）, but the other animals found more inspiration in Boxer's strength and his never-failing cry of "I will work harder!"

[P03] The corn ration（配给） was cut very much, and it was said that more potatoes would be given out to make up for it. Then they found that most of the potato crop had been frosted（结霜的） in the clamps（夹子）, which had not been covered thickly（厚厚地） enough. The potatoes had gone soft and lost their colour, and only a few could be eaten. For days at a time the animals had nothing to eat but chaff（谷壳） and mangels（饲料甜菜）. Starvation（饥饿） seemed to stare（盯着） them in the face. It was vitally（至关重要） necessary to hide this fact from the outside world.

[P04] The people were bold because the windmill fell. They made up new lies about Animal Farm. They said all the animals were dying（垂死） of hunger and disease. They said the animals fought each other and even ate their own kind and killed their babies. Napoleon knew well the bad results if people learned the truth about the food. He decided to use Mr. Whymper to spread a different impression. Before this, the animals had little or no contact with Whymper on his weekly visits. Now, however, a few chosen animals, mostly（大多数） sheep, were told to say in a casual（随意的） way, where he could hear, that rations（配给） had been increased.

[P05] Also, Napoleon ordered the almost empty（空的） bins in the store-shed to be filled nearly to the top with sand, and then covered with the little grain（谷物） and meal left. On some good excuse Whymper was led through the store-shed and allowed to see the bins for a moment. He was fooled, and went on telling the outside world that there was no food shortage on Animal Farm. Nevertheless（然而）, by the end of January it was clear that they must get more grain from somewhere. In these days Napoleon seldom appeared in public, but spent all his time in the farmhouse（农舍）, which was guarded at each door by fierce-looking dogs.

[P06] When he did come out, it was in a ceremonial（仪式的，正式的） way, with six dogs as escort（护送，陪同） who closely（紧密地） surrounded（包围） him and growled（咆哮） if anyone came too near. Often he did not even appear on Sunday mornings, but gave his orders through one of the other pigs, usually Squealer. One Sunday morning Squealer frequently（经常，频繁地） announced that the hens, who had just come in to lay again, must give up their eggs. Napoleon had accepted, through Whymper, a contract for four hundred eggs a week. The price of these would pay for enough grain and meal to keep the farm going till summer came and conditions were easier. When the hens heard this, they raised a terrible outcry（抗议）.

[P07] They had been warned that this sacrifice（牺牲） might be needed, but had not believed it would happen. They were getting their clutches（抓紧，魔爪） ready for the spring sitting, and protested（抗议） that to take the eggs away now was murder. For the first time since the expulsion（驱逐） of Jones, there was something like an uprising（起义）. Led by three young Black Minorca（米诺卡鸡） pullets（小母鸡）, the hens tried to stop Napoleon's wishes. Their method was to fly up to the rafters（椽子） and lay their eggs there, which smashed（粉碎） on the floor. Napoleon acted quickly and without mercy（仁慈）. He ordered the hens' rations stopped, and decreed（下令，判决） that any animal giving so much as a grain of corn to a hen should be punished by death.

[P08] The dogs saw to it that these orders were carried out. For five days the hens held out, then they gave in and went back to their nesting boxes. Nine hens had died in the meantime（同时，其间）. Their bodies were buried in the orchard（果园）, and it was given out that they had died of coccidiosis（球虫病）. Whymper heard nothing of this affair（事情，事务）, and the eggs were duly（按时地，适当地） delivered（递送）, a grocer（杂货商）'s van（货车） driving up to the farm once a week to take them away.

[P09] People said he was hiding on one of the neighbouring farms, either Foxwood（狐林） or Pinchfield（窄地）. By this time Napoleon was on slightly（稍微） better terms with the other farmers than before. It happened that there was in the yard a pile of timber（木材） stacked（堆叠） there ten years earlier when a beech（山毛榉） spinney（小树林） was cleared. It was well seasoned, and Whymper had advised Napoleon to sell it; both Mr. Pilkington and Mr. Frederick were eager（渴望） to buy it. Napoleon was hesitating（犹豫，迟疑） between the two, unable（无法） to decide. It was noticed that whenever he seemed about to agree with Frederick, Snowball was said to be hiding at Foxwood, while, when he leaned toward Pilkington, Snowball was said to be at Pinchfield. Suddenly, early in the spring, an alarming thing was discovered.

[P10] Snowball was secretly（秘密地） visiting the farm at night! The animals were so worried that they could hardly sleep in their stalls（畜栏）. Every night, it was said, he came creeping（爬行，蔓延） in under cover of darkness and did all kinds of bad things. He stole the corn, knocked over the milk-pails（桶）, broke the eggs, stepped heavily（沉重地） on the seedbeds（苗床）, and bit the bark off the fruit trees. Whenever anything went wrong, it became usual to blame（责怪，归咎） it on Snowball. If a window was broken or a drain（排水） was blocked up, someone was sure to say that Snowball had come in the night and done it, and when the key of the store-shed was lost, the whole farm was sure that Snowball had thrown it down the well.

[P11] Curiously（好奇地） enough, they still believed this even after the lost key was found under a sack（麻袋） of meal. The cows all said together that Snowball came into their stalls and milked them while they slept. The rats, which had been a problem that winter, were also said to be in league（联盟） with Snowball. Napoleon ordered that there should be a full inquiry（询问，调查） into Snowball's activities. With his dogs beside him, he set out and made a careful tour of the farm buildings, the other animals following at a respectful（恭敬的） distance.

[P12] At every few steps Napoleon stopped and snuffed（嗅） the ground for traces（痕迹） of Snowball's footsteps, which, he said, he could detect（发现，察觉） by the smell. He snuffed in every corner, in the barn（谷仓）, in the cow-shed, in the henhouses（鸡舍）, in the vegetable garden, and found traces of Snowball almost everywhere. He would put his snout（口鼻部） to the ground, give several deep sniffs（嗅）, and cry out in a terrible voice, "Snowball! He has been here! I can smell him distinctly（清楚地）!" and at the word "Snowball" all the dogs let out blood-curdling（凝结，令人毛骨悚然） growls（咆哮） and showed their side teeth. The animals were thoroughly（彻底） frightened. It seemed to them as though Snowball were some kind of invisible（看不见的） influence, filling the air about them and threatening（威胁的） them with all kinds of dangers.

[P13] In the evening Squealer called them together, and with a worried look told them, "Comrades（同志们）, I have serious news.""Comrades!" cried Squealer, making little nervous jumps, "a most terrible thing has been discovered. Snowball has sold himself to Frederick of Pinchfield Farm, who is even now planning（计划） to attack us and take our farm away! Snowball will act as his guide when the attack begins. But there is worse. We had thought that Snowball's uprising was caused simply by his vanity（虚荣） and ambition. But we were wrong, comrades. Do you know what the real reason was?

[P14] Snowball was working with Jones from the very start! He was Jones's secret agent all the time. Papers he left behind prove it, and we have only just found them. To my mind this explains a great deal, comrades. Did we not see how he tried—luckily without success—to get us beaten at the Battle of the Cowshed（牛棚）?" The animals were stupefied（惊呆的）. This was a wickedness（邪恶） far worse than Snowball's destruction（破坏，毁灭） of the windmill. But it was some minutes before they could take it in. They all remembered how they had seen Snowball charging（冲锋，收费） ahead of them at the Battle of the Cowshed, how he had rallied（团结） and encouraged them at every turn, and how he had not stopped even when the pellets（颗粒） from Jones's gun had wounded his back.

[P15] At first it was hard to see how this fit with his being on Jones's side. Even Boxer, who seldom asked questions, was puzzled（困惑）. He lay down, tucked（塞进） his fore（前部） hoofs（蹄） under him, shut his eyes, and with a hard effort put his thoughts into words. But it was some minutes before they could fully take it in. "I do not believe that," he said. "Snowball fought bravely（勇敢地） at the Battle of the Cowshed. I saw him myself. Did we not give him 'Animal Hero, first Class,' right afterwards（后来）?" "That was our mistake, comrade（同志）. For we know now—it is all written down in the secret papers we have found—that in truth he was trying to lure（引诱，诱惑） us to our doom（厄运）." "But he was wounded," said Boxer.

[P16] "We all saw him running（跑步） with blood." "That was the plan!" cried Squealer. "Jones's shot only grazed（放牧） him. I could show you in his own writing, if you could read. The plot（阴谋） was for Snowball, at the critical（关键的，危急的） moment, to give the signal（信号） to run away and leave the field to the enemy. And he nearly succeeded -- I will say, comrades, he WOULD have succeeded without our heroic（英勇） Leader, Comrade Napoleon. Do you not remember how, just when Jones and his men got inside the yard, Snowball suddenly turned and ran, and many animals followed him?

[P17] And do you not remember, too, that it was just at that moment, when panic was spreading and all seemed lost, that Comrade Napoleon sprang（跳起） forward with a cry of 'Death to Humanity（人类）!' and sank his teeth in Jones's leg? Surely you remember THAT, comrades?" exclaimed（惊叫，呼喊） Squealer, jumping from side to side. Now when Squealer described the scene so clearly, it seemed to the animals that they did remember it. At any rate（比率）, they remembered that at the critical moment of the battle Snowball had turned to run away. But Boxer was still a little uneasy（不安）. "I do not believe that Snowball was a traitor at the beginning," Boxer said.he said finally.

[P18] "What he has done since is different. But I believe at the Battle of the Cowshed he was a good comrade. Our Leader, Comrade Napoleon."Our Leader, Comrade Napoleon," announced Squealer, speaking very slowly and firmly（坚定地）, "has stated categorically（明确地）--categorically, comrade--that Snowball was Jones's agent from the very beginning--yes, and long before the uprising was thought of." "Ah, that is different!" said Boxer. "If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right." "That is the true spirit, comrade!" cried Squealer, but it was noticed he cast（投，扔，抛） a very ugly look at Boxer with his little twinkling（闪烁） eyes. He turned to go, then paused（暂停，停顿） and added impressively（令人印象深刻地）: "I warn every animal on this farm to keep his eyes very wide open.

[P19] For we have reason to think that some of Snowball's secret agents are hiding among us right now!" Four days later, in the late afternoon, Napoleon ordered all the animals to gather（收集） in the yard. When they were all together, Napoleon came out of the farmhouse, wearing both his medals (for he had recently given himself "Animal Hero, First Class" and "Animal Hero, Second Class"), with his nine huge dogs jumping round him and making growls that sent shivers（颤抖） down all the animals' spines（刺）. They all crouched（蹲下，蜷缩） silently（默默地） in their places, seeming to know ahead of time that some terrible thing was about to happen. Napoleon stood sternly（严厉地） looking over his audience; then he let out a high-pitched（投掷） whimper（呜咽）.

[P20] At once the dogs rushed forward, caught four of the pigs by the ear and pulled them, squealing（尖叫） with pain and terror（恐怖）, to Napoleon's feet immediately. The pigs' ears were bleeding, and for a few moments the dogs seemed to go quite mad. To everyone's amazement（惊讶，惊奇）, three of them threw themselves upon Boxer. Boxer saw them coming and put out his great hoof（蹄）, caught a dog in mid-air, and pinned（固定） him to the ground. The dog shrieked（尖叫） for mercy and the other two ran away. Boxer looked at Napoleon to know whether he should crush（压碎） the dog to death or let it go.

[P21] Napoleon seemed to change face, and sharply（尖锐地） ordered Boxer to let the dog go, so Boxer lifted his hoof, and the dog slunk（溜走） away, bruised and howling（咆哮，嚎叫）. Presently（不久） the tumult（喧哗，骚动） died down. Presently the tumult died down. The four pigs waited, trembling（发抖）, with guilt（罪行） on their faces. Napoleon now called on them to confess（坦白） their crimes. They were the same four pigs who had protested when Napoleon abolished（废除） the Sunday Meetings. Without further（进一步） prompting they confessed（坦白） that they had been secretly in touch with Snowball since his expulsion, that they had helped him destroy the windmill, and that they had agreed to hand over Animal Farm to Mr.

[P22] Frederick. They added that Snowball had privately（私下地） admitted（承认） to them that he had been Jones's secret agent for years past. When they finished their confession（坦白，承认）, the dogs promptly（立即） tore their throats out, and in a terrible voice Napoleon demanded（要求） whether any other animal had anything to confess. The three hens who had been the ringleaders（头目） in the attempted（试图，尝试） uprising over the eggs now came forward and stated that Snowball had appeared to them in a dream and incited（煽动，激起） them to disobey（违抗） Napoleon's orders. They, too, were slaughtered（被屠杀）. Then a goose came forward and confessed to having secreted six ears of corn during the last year's harvest and eaten them in the night.

[P23] Then a sheep confessed to having urinated（撒尿） in the drinking pool—urged（催促） to do this, so she said, by Snowball—and two other sheep confessed to having murdered an old ram（公羊）, a devoted（忠诚的） follower of Napoleon, by chasing（追赶） him round and round a bonfire（篝火） when he was suffering from a cough. They were all killed on the spot（地点）. And so the tale of confessions（坦白） and killings（杀戮） went on, until a pile of dead bodies lay before Napoleon's feet and the air was heavy with the smell of blood, unknown（未知的） there since the expulsion of Jones. When it was over, the remaining animals, except the pigs and dogs, crept（爬行） away in a body.

[P24] They were shaken and miserable（悲惨的）. They did not know which was worse—the treachery（背叛） of the animals who had joined Snowball, or the cruel punishment（惩罚） they had just seen. In the old days there had often been bloodshed（流血，杀戮） just as terrible, but it seemed far worse now that it was happening among themselves. Since Jones had left, no animal had killed another. They made their way to the little knoll（小丘） where the half-finished windmill stood, and with one accord（一致） they all lay down as though huddling（挤在一起） together for warmth（温暖）—Clover, Muriel, Benjamin, the cows, the sheep, and a whole flock（羊群） of geese and hens—everyone except the cat, who had suddenly disappeared before Napoleon ordered the animals to assemble（集合）.

[P25] For some time nobody spoke. Only Boxer was still on his feet. He moved about, swishing（嗖嗖声） his long black tail against his sides, and now and then gave a little whinny（嘶鸣） of surprise. At last he said: "I do not understand it. I would not have believed that such things could happen on our farm. It must be due（由于） to some fault in ourselves. The answer, as I see it, is to work harder. From now on I shall get up a full hour earlier in the mornings." And he moved off at his heavy trot（疾走） and made for the quarry.

[P26] Having got there, he collected two loads（负载） of stone one after the other and dragged（拖） them down to the windmill before he went to rest for the night, while the animals huddled（蜷缩，挤在一起） about Clover, not speaking. The animals huddled about Clover, not speaking. The knoll where they were lying（躺） gave them a wide prospect（前景） across the countryside. Most of Animal Farm was within their view--the long pasture（牧场） stretching（伸展） down to the main road, the hayfield（干草地）, the spinney, the drinking pool, the ploughed fields where the young wheat was thick and green, and the red roofs of the farm buildings with the smoke curling（卷曲，缭绕） from the chimneys（烟囱）. It was a clear spring evening. The grass and the bursting（爆裂） hedges（树篱） were gilded（镀金的，金色的） by the level rays（光线） of the sun.

[P27] The farm had never seemed so desirable（可取的，令人满意的） to the animals--and with surprise they remembered that it was their own farm, every inch their own property（财产）. As Clover looked down the hillside（山坡，山腰） her eyes filled with tears. If she could have spoken her thoughts, she would have said this was not what they had aimed at when they set themselves years ago to work for the overthrow（推翻，打倒） of the human race. These scenes of terror and slaughter（屠杀） were not what they had looked forward to on that night when old Major first stirred（搅动） them to uprising. If she herself had had any picture of the future, it had been of a society of animals set free from hunger and the whip, all equal, each working according to his capacity（能力）, the strong protecting the weak, as she had protected the lost group of baby ducklings（小鸭） with her foreleg（前腿） on the night of Major's speech.

[P28] Instead—she did not know why—they had come to a time when no one dared speak his mind, when fierce dogs roamed（漫游） everywhere, and when you had to watch your comrades torn apart（分开） after confessing（承认，坦白） to shocking crimes. She never thought of uprising or disobedience（不服从，违抗）. She knew they were far better off than in the days of Jones, and that above all they must prevent（阻止） the return of the humans. Whatever happened she would remain faithful（忠诚）, work hard, obey（服从） orders, and accept Napoleon's leadership（领导）.

[P29] But still, it was not for this that she and all the other animals had hoped and worked so hard. It was not for this that they had built the windmill and faced the bullets（子弹） of Jones's gun. Such were her thoughts, though she lacked the words to express them. At last, feeling this to be in some way a substitute（替代） for the words she was unable to find, she began to sing 'animals of England'. The other animals sitting round her took it up, and they sang it three times over--very tunefully（悦耳地）, but slowly and mournfully（悲伤）, in a way they had never sung it before. They had just finished singing it for the third time when Squealer, with two dogs beside him, came up to them with the air of having something important to say.

[P30] He announced that, by a special decree（法令） of Comrade Napoleon, 'animals of England' had been abolished. From then on, no one was allowed to sing it. The animals were taken aback（吃惊，猝不及防）. "Why?" cried Muriel. "Muriel cried, 'It's no longer needed, comrade,'"said Squealer stiffly（僵硬地）. "'animals of England' was the song of the uprising. But the uprising is now complete. The traitors were executed（执行，处决） this afternoon. That was the final act. The enemy outside and inside has been defeated. In this song we expressed our longing for a better society in days to come. But that society has now been established（建立，确立）. Clearly this song has no purpose now." Clearly, frightened though they were, some animals might have protested, but just then the sheep began bleating "Four legs good, two legs bad,"which went on for several minutes and ended the discussion, so 'animals of England' was heard no more. So 'animals of England' was heard no more.

[P31] Instead, Minimus the poet had written another song. It began: Animal Farm, Animal Farm, Never through me shalt（将） thou（你） come to harm! The animals sang it every Sunday morning after they raised the flag. But somehow（不知怎的） neither the words nor the tune（曲调） ever seemed to the animals to be as good as 'animals of England'.
